title: Kth largest element in an array
md:
## The idea

Keep the **k largest values seen so far** in a min-heap. The heap's smallest value is the k-th largest so far. A new value only matters if it beats that smallest value.

## Step by step

1. For each value: if the heap has fewer than k items, add it.
2. Otherwise, if the value is bigger than the heap's top, replace the top with it.
3. At the end, the top is the answer.

## Worked example

**Input:** nums = [3, 2, 1, 5, 6, 4], k = 2

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 3, 2 | heap {2, 3} |
| 1 | not > 2 → ignore |
| 5 | replace 2 → {3, 5} |
| 6 | replace 3 → {5, 6} |
| 4 | not > 5 → ignore |

**Result:** 5

## Cost

O(n log k) time, O(k) memory. (Quickselect: O(n) on average, if asked.)

## The code (C#, compiled and tested against every part of the question)

```csharp
// LeetCode 215 — the k-th largest value (k = 1 is the maximum).
public static class KthLargest {
    public static int Find(int[] nums, int k) {
        if (nums == null || k < 1 || k > nums.Length) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(k));
        // Keep the k largest values seen so far in a MIN-heap. Its smallest element is the k-th largest.
        var heap = new PriorityQueue<int, int>();
        foreach (int x in nums) {
            if (heap.Count < k) heap.Enqueue(x, x);
            else if (x > heap.Peek()) heap.EnqueueDequeue(x, x);   // x beats the weakest of the top k
        }
        return heap.Peek();
    }
}
```

## Likely follow-up questions

**Q: Distinct values only?**

Ask. Distinct means de-duplicate first.

**Q: Complexity?**

Heap: O(n log k). Quickselect: O(n) average, O(n²) worst; random pivot makes the worst case unlikely.

**Q: Which would you pick?**

Heap for streams or small k; quickselect when the whole array is in memory and k is large.

**Q: Many threads add values.**

Each thread keeps its own top-k heap; merge the heaps at the end.

**Q: A stream that never ends.**

Keep the k-heap forever — LeetCode 703. Across machines, each keeps a local top k and a coordinator merges them.
